title: API 570 Training in Billings, MT: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep for Billings and Laurel piping inspectors: self-paced online with instructor Q&A, covering coker lines, CUI on traced pipe and CML intervals.
h1: API 570 Training in Billings, Montana: Online Exam Prep for Refinery and Terminal Piping Inspectors
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors from Laurel to east Billings

Piping is where most of an inspection department's hours go in Billings. Three refineries sit within a short drive of each other along the Yellowstone, the CHS plant at Laurel and the Phillips 66 and Par Montana plants on the south-east and north-east edges of the city, and each is fed and emptied by pipelines that meet in the same stretch of valley. Unit piping, pipe racks, tank farm manifolds, loading racks and the lines between them add up to a great many condition monitoring locations, and API 570 is the code owners use to decide when each one is next measured.

Atlantis NDT's API 570 course is an online exam-preparation course that you take at your own pace, with an instructor answering questions as they come up. You start when you enrol. There is no Atlantis classroom in Billings. API, through its Individual Certification Programs, administers the Piping Inspector examination at Prometric test centres and issues the certificate to those who pass; the course gives you the knowledge and the open-book speed that the day requires.

Crude in, products out: the lines that tie the plants together

The pipelines around Billings explain much of the piping an inspector meets inside the fence, because each delivers into, or draws from, manifolds, meters and tanks on refinery ground.

  • Front Range Pipeline (CHS). More than 320 miles of crude line in Montana, carrying more than 65,000 barrels a day from the Canadian border to the Laurel and Billings refineries, with storage at Laurel, Santa Rita and Cut Bank.
  • Silvertip pipeline (Par Pacific). A 70-mile, 55,000 barrel-a-day crude line, wholly owned since the 2023 purchase, that gives the Par refinery direct access to Rocky Mountain grades.
  • Express pipeline (Enbridge). Western Canadian crude from Hardisty, Alberta to Casper, Wyoming, delivering into Montana and Wyoming, with storage terminals at Buffalo and Edgar in Montana.
  • Cenex Pipeline (CHS). Refined products from the Laurel and Billings refineries to terminals at Glendive, Minot and Fargo, more than 773 miles and an average of 43,000 barrels a day.
  • Yellowstone pipeline. A 750-mile, 65,000 barrel-a-day products line from Billings to eastern Washington, in which Par Pacific holds a 40% interest.

These are pipelines regulated under federal hazardous liquid rules, not process piping, and API 570 does not govern the line itself. What matters for the exam is the boundary: the in-plant receiving and dispatch piping, the tank farm headers and the unit feed lines on the refinery side of that boundary are API 570 systems, and the code's scope section is where a candidate learns how owners draw the line.

Coker and gas oil piping: sulfidation and erosion

EIA's survey for the start of 2026 lists delayed cokers at Phillips 66 (20,050 barrels per stream day) and CHS (16,000), a fluid coker at Par Montana (10,000), and gas oil hydrotreating at Phillips 66 and CHS. Hot, sulfur-bearing gas oil and residue lines are the textbook setting for sulfidation, and the coker's slurries and solids bring erosion at elbows, tees and control valve outlets. Both are on the API 570 exam: the Body of Knowledge lists fifteen RP 571 sections for piping, among them sulfidation (3.61), erosion and erosion-corrosion (3.27), hydrochloric acid corrosion (3.37), sour water corrosion (3.58), amine stress corrosion cracking (3.3), caustic corrosion and caustic cracking (3.14 and 3.15), chloride stress corrosion cracking (3.17), mechanical fatigue including vibration (3.43), soil corrosion (3.57) and microbiologically influenced corrosion (3.45).

Note what is missing. High-temperature hydrogen attack and high-temperature H2/H2S corrosion are on the API 510 list but not on the API 570 list, so a Billings candidate who spends the working week on hydrotreater piping should not spend study time on them for this exam. Sulfidation, by contrast, rewards detail: in hot carbon steel circuits, a fitting or spool made from steel with low silicon content can thin much faster than the pipe either side of it, which is why many owners inspect such circuits component by component rather than trusting one reading per spool.

Heated asphalt and residue lines through a Montana winter

Asphalt is a large product here. EIA lists asphalt and road oil capacity of 19,800 barrels per stream day at CHS Laurel and 14,500 at Par Montana, and Calumet's smaller plant at Great Falls adds 4,700. Asphalt and heavy residue are moved hot, so the lines that carry them are insulated and traced, often for their whole length, and they cool and reheat whenever a unit trips or a rundown stops.

That makes corrosion under insulation (RP 571 section 3.22) the piping mechanism a Billings inspector deals with most outside the process units. Water gets under jacketing at damaged seams, at supports and at insulation penetrations, and in a cold climate snow, ice and meltwater test every weak point in the cladding. RP 571 explains which temperature ranges make carbon and stainless steels susceptible and why cycling service is worse than steady service. API 570 then tells the inspector how to plan for it: it lists the locations where damage is most likely, ties the extent of inspection to the piping class and the condition found, and expects insulation to be removed where the risk calls for it. Learn that method and where it sits in the code; the percentages and extents are in the text of your edition and should be read there, not memorised from a summary.

Atmospheric corrosion (3.8) belongs with it: uninsulated pipe on racks and at supports suffers where water sits, and the external visual inspection the code requires is meant to catch it.

CML circuits, injection points and dead legs on a Billings unit

A piping inspector's job turns on three ideas the exam tests directly. The first is the circuit: piping of similar material, service and expected corrosion, grouped so that its condition monitoring locations represent it. A CML programme is only as good as the choice of locations, and RP 574 is the reference for where readings belong: elbows and tees, downstream of control valves, at changes of velocity and at points where flow can stagnate.

The second is the injection point. Crude units add caustic and corrosion inhibitor, and overhead systems on cokers and catalytic crackers take wash water; where a chemical enters a hotter or faster stream, corrosion can be far worse than in the rest of the line. API 570 treats injection points as separate circuits, defines how far upstream and downstream of the point the circuit runs, and asks for thickness readings and, where warranted, other examination along that length. The limits are written in the code and the course takes you to them; learn to find them quickly in your edition rather than carrying a remembered figure into the exam.

The third is the dead leg: a branch with no flow, such as a bypass, a drain or a spare connection, where water and solids collect. In Billings a dead leg also freezes, which is a reason operators give for removing them as well as a reason inspectors watch them. API 570 expects dead legs to be identified and inspected, at the stagnant end and at the connection to the live line, and favours removal of those that serve no purpose.

Worked example: a coker gas oil line where the structural minimum governs

The Body of Knowledge asks you to calculate corrosion rates and remaining life, and to set the thickness and external inspection intervals from API 570 section 6.3.3 and its table of maximum intervals. Take an NPS 6 carbon steel line, outside diameter 6.625 in., in hot gas oil service that the owner has classed as Class 2. Design pressure is 600 psi, and the question gives S = 20,000 psi at design temperature, E = 1.0 (seamless), W = 1.0 and Y = 0.4. The owner's structural minimum for this size is 0.110 in. Readings at the CML were 0.276 in. when the line was installed, 0.240 in. six years before the latest survey, and 0.205 in. now, 14 years after installation.

  1. Pressure design thickness, B31.3 304.1.2. t = PD ÷ 2(SEW + PY) = 600 × 6.625 ÷ 2(20,000 + 240) = 3,975 ÷ 40,480 = 0.098 in.
  2. Required thickness. The larger of 0.098 in. and the 0.110 in. structural minimum, so 0.110 in. governs. Many owners start their structural minimums from the defaults tabulated in RP 574, which is part of the exam.
  3. Corrosion rates, API 570 7.1.2. Long-term: (0.276 − 0.205) ÷ 14 = 0.00507 in. a year. Short-term: (0.240 − 0.205) ÷ 6 = 0.00583 in. a year. Nothing suggests the process has eased, so take the faster short-term rate.
  4. Remaining life, 7.2. (0.205 − 0.110) ÷ 0.00583 = 16.3 years.
  5. Intervals. Half the remaining life is 8.1 years; the table maximum for Class 2 thickness measurement is 10 years, so the next thickness reading is due within 8.1 years. The Class 2 external visual inspection stays at the 5-year maximum, which does not depend on remaining life.

Two exam habits come out of this. If you had used the 0.098 in. pressure design thickness, the remaining life would have looked like 18.3 years, which shows why the structural minimum must be checked first. Had the long-term rate been the faster one, you would have weighed it the same way: the code leaves the choice to the inspector, who selects the rate that best reflects current service.

Getting to API 570 eligibility from a Billings piping job

The experience rules are the same shape as for API 510, applied to piping. A bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, or three years of technical military service, needs one year supervising or performing piping inspection; a two-year degree or certificate needs two years in design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of piping including one year of inspection; a high school diploma needs three years and no formal education five or more. The experience must come from the last 10 years while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency, and API verifies what you document. The API 570 certification requirements page covers the detail.

Welders and pipefitters often have the construction and repair years already. City College at Montana State University Billings lists refinery piping fabrication and repair and overland pipeline construction among the fields its welding and metal fabrication graduates go into, and the Section IX and RP 577 parts of the exam are familiar ground for people from that work; the inspection year usually comes from a move into a QC or inspection role. NDT technicians who take thickness readings on CMLs and scan hot lines with UT for a contractor are performing inspection work, and the NDT training in Billings page covers the method certifications behind it. Pipeline technicians are the uncertain case: integrity work on a regulated line is valuable, but API decides whether it matches the piping the code describes, so plant piping experience is the safer basis for an application.

Studying B31.3 and B16.5 between Billings shifts

The open-book half of the API 570 exam is where piping candidates win or lose time, and most of it lives in tables. Practise until each of these is a reflex in the PDF: the B31.3 Table A-1 allowable stresses and Table A-1B quality factors, the preheat table at 330.1.1, the thermal expansion table in Appendix C, the leak test clauses at 345.4 and 345.5, the blank thickness formula at 304.5.3, and the B16.5 pressure-temperature ratings by material group and class. The self-paced course lets you spend more hours where you are slowest, and when a table seems to give two answers you send the question and the instructor walks you through the reading.

Shift workers at the refineries tend to do better with short, regular sessions than with long weekends: one table or one RP 574 chapter per session, with a timed set of practice questions at the end of each week. Save the full timed papers, which copy the real split between closed-book and open-book questions, for the last stretch before your exam window.

Sponsoring piping inspectors from a Billings refinery, pipeline or contractor

Refineries, pipeline operators and inspection contractors can sponsor several API 570 candidates together, and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually, so the employer's useful contribution is a clear record of each person's inspection experience and a study plan that does not collide with outage season. Pair the exam preparation with CML programme work where you can: a candidate who has helped set up circuits on a real unit reads API 570 and RP 574 very differently from one who has only collected readings.

faq.q: Can I take an API 570 class in person in Billings?
faq.a: Not with Atlantis. There is no Atlantis classroom in Billings; the course is online and self-paced, with an instructor answering your questions, and you can begin when you enrol. The examination itself is sat in person at a Prometric test centre after API has approved your application, so plan for the trip if the nearest centre with a seat is out of town.

faq.q: Does integrity work on a crude or products pipeline count as API 570 experience?
faq.a: It may or may not. API 570 is written for in-service metallic process piping, and API decides whether the experience you describe matches what the code covers. Inspection of the receiving, dispatch and tank farm piping inside a refinery or terminal is the clearer case. If most of your years are on regulated pipelines, describe the work precisely on the application and ask API before you rely on it.

faq.q: Is high-temperature hydrogen attack on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Not in the current Body of Knowledge. The piping exam draws on fifteen listed RP 571 sections, including sulfidation, erosion, CUI, sour water corrosion and amine cracking, but high-temperature hydrogen attack and high-temperature H2/H2S corrosion are listed for API 510 rather than API 570. If you inspect hydrotreater piping at work, keep learning them for the job; just do not spend API 570 study time on them.

faq.q: What does API 570 expect at injection points?
faq.a: It treats each injection point as its own circuit, sets how far upstream and downstream of the point that circuit extends, and asks for thickness measurement and, where the inspector judges it necessary, other examination within those limits. The exact distances are in the code text of your edition. The course shows you where they are and how exam questions use them, so that you read them from the PDF rather than from memory.

faq.q: How should I practise the B16.5 flange rating questions?
faq.a: Work them in the PDF, timed. Identify the material group from the material table first, then read the pressure-temperature rating for the class and temperature, interpolating where the question requires it. The Body of Knowledge also asks for the most economical flange class for a given pressure and temperature, which is the same lookup run in reverse. Expect to make every mistake once in practice so that you make none on the day.

faq.q: I work at a Billings refinery. Should I take API 510 or API 570 first?
faq.a: Usually the one that matches the inspection you already do, because that experience is what qualifies you. Inspectors who spend most of their time on CML programmes and unit piping tend to start with API 570; those who open vessels at turnarounds tend to start with API 510. Holding either one also qualifies you automatically to sit API 580 if your employer runs a risk-based inspection programme.

faq.q: Can our refinery or inspection contractor enrol a group of piping inspectors?
faq.a: Yes. A group can be enrolled together and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate studies at their own pace and asks the instructor questions individually, which works for crews on different rotations. Every person still applies to API separately and books their own Prometric appointment, so keep each candidate's experience records current before the application goes in.
